newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-REDS FIRE MANAGER RAY KNIGHT.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-REDS FIRE MANAGER RAY KNIGHT.

text.p: The Cincinnati Reds fired manager Ray Knight on Friday and replaced him temporarily with consultant Jack McKeon.

The Reds have struggled on the field and numerous reports have claimed that Knight lost the respect of his players. The team has lost five of its last six games and 10 of 15 to stand at 43-56, 9-1/2 games behind the National League Central-leading Houston Astros.

This year Knight was suspended three games for a run-in with umpire Jerry Layne in May, assumed third-base coaching duties for two weeks from Joel Youngblood and had a heated confrontation with veteran pitcher Mike Morgan in a game.

Knight was in his second season as Reds manager after two-plus years as an assistant coach. It was his first managerial experience. He played in the majors from 1974-88 and serving as a broadcaster for ESPN from 1989 until becoming a Reds coach in May 1993.

Last year, Knight had the Reds within four games of the division lead as late as September 8th, but they lost eight of the next nine and wound up finishing 81-81, seven games behind first-place St. Louis and nine in back of wild card Los Angeles.
Knight was a career .271 hitter as a third baseman and first baseman with Cincinnati, Houston, the New York Mets, Baltimore and Detroit. He is mulling a consultant position with the Reds.
McKeon has been with the Reds since 1993, working with general manager Jim Bowden on special assignments and assisting in trades and player evaluations.
"I've been in this situation many times, I've replaced people and I've been replaced," said McKeon.

"Out of loyalty to (owner) Marge (Schott) and (managing executive) John (Allen) and Jim, I've decided to take this job. I still think we can turn this thing around. We can pick up a game a week the rest of the season. I think we can still do it."

McKeon, nicknamed "Trader Jack" for his tendency to make deals at any time of the day, has previously managed Kansas City (1973-75), Oakland (1977-78) and San Diego (1988-90), while also serving as the Padres' general manager from 1980-90.
His .541 winning percentage (193-164) from 1988-90 is the best in Padres history.
This is the second managerial change in the majors this season. Kansas City replaced Bob Boone with Tony Muser on July 9th.
